article_content: The Connecticut State Police will release its report on the Sandy Hook Elementary School shootings on Friday. The report, which spans several thousand pages, encompasses text, photographs, and 911 calls from the day of the tragic shootings. According to Lt. J. Paul Vance, the spokesman for the state police, 'the report has been redacted according to law.' Previously, authorities released audio recordings of 911 calls from that day, providing insight into the horrific events at Sandy Hook Elementary School. Prosecutors' summary earlier this month described the gunman, Adam Lanza, as being obsessed with mass murders, yet concluded that Lanza's motives for the massacre might never be fully understood. On December 14, 2012, Lanza, 20 years old, killed 20 first-graders and six school staff members using a semi-automatic rifle at the elementary school. Beforehand, he killed his mother inside their home. Lanza, who had significant mental health issues, committed suicide with a handgun as police arrived. The report is available at: www.ct.gov/StatePoliceNewtownReport.
